analysis: The trial completed successfully with host validation macro HR@10 of 0.4100: Movies_and_TV 0.450, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.405, Electronics 0.330, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.455. This is 0.0088 above the supplied pooling model's 0.4012, but 0.095 below the supplied SASRec baseline's 0.505. Adding sequential context produced a modest aggregate improvement, insufficient to recover baseline performance. Electronics remained the weakest category. These results do not isolate whether the remaining limitation comes from pooling, the pairwise objective, prefix sampling, or optimization; per-category pooling results were not supplied, so category-specific improvements cannot be established.
code_summary: One independently trained network per category adds learned position embeddings and two pre-normalized causal Transformer blocks (128 dimensions, four heads, 256-dimensional GELU feed-forward layers, dropout 0.25) before history pooling. The encoder combines the contextualized last item, mean, and two learned recency-aware attention pools into a normalized user representation. Scores use normalized learned output embeddings, a learned scale, and jointly trained item biases. Training retains sampled prefixes, 64 sampled negatives, a pairwise softplus loss with equal uniform and detached hard-negative weighting, and AdamW. Validation selects one checkpoint per category; the generated predictor loads the matching architecture and routes each dataset to exactly one checkpoint. No ensemble or separately fitted scoring component is used.
